files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
Thumbnails made in the viewer now show the model as its file has it, whatever wireframe, exploded view, transform or animation state the viewer was in, and exports from exploded view have the parts together. The top bar stays usable while a model loads, and every control in the tools panel works from the keyboard and is announced to screen readers. Textures named by a path above the model's folder, such as `..\..\textures\wood.jpg`, are found beside the model. Every route that changes data now checks Nextcloud's request token.

### Fixed
- A thumbnail made in the viewer could show how one user was viewing the model, and it is shown to everyone who can see the file. The viewer makes the thumbnail from the model it has open, half a second after it opens, and several tools change that model: with Wireframe on, the thumbnail was a wireframe; in Exploded view, its parts were flung apart and framed small; after the transform gizmo had turned or stretched the model, it was drawn that way; while a clipping plane or box was open, the back of an open surface showed; an animated model was caught at whatever frame its animation had reached; and a G-code file opened with Single colour picked was drawn in that colour, where the same file got the gradient when Files made its thumbnail. Each tool now keeps a record of what it changed, and the thumbnail is drawn from the model as the file has it, as it already was for Clay, Normals and X-ray: no wireframe (a material the file itself makes wireframe stays one), the parts together, the model as loaded, the pose the file opens in, and the G-code gradient. The viewer keeps showing what you chose. Thumbnails already stored are not remade; one goes when its file changes.
- Exports made in Exploded view wrote the parts where the view had moved them, so an STL, OBJ, PLY, 3MF, GLB or USDZ file, and the file Send to Slicer sends, had the parts flung apart. Exports now have the parts together, in every format; a model turned or moved with the transform gizmo is still exported as you placed it, and an animated model in the pose it is in. Exporting a GLB, USDZ or 3MF no longer drops a paused animation's parts back to where the file puts them.
- With Wireframe on, the next model you opened was drawn solid while the switch still read on, and Exploded view stayed "Active" with the next model's parts together. Both now carry on to the next model, as the Clay, Normals and X-ray shading does; Exploded view turns off for a model it cannot take apart, and the camera frames the parts as they are shown. The model statistics are those of the model with its parts together, also when it opens exploded. Wireframe also reaches the parts of a model that have more than one material, which it skipped.
- Switching G-code from Single colour back to Gradient tinted the gradient with the single colour, and a toolpath opened while Single colour was picked turned black on the switch. The gradient now comes back as it was.
- While a model loaded, the loading screen covered the top bar as well as the 3D view, so Help, the Tools button and the view actions could not be pressed until the model arrived, which for a large file is the whole wait. The loading screen now covers only the 3D view, and the bar stays usable, with Cancel loading still on the loading screen.
- Models whose textures are named by a path relative to the project rather than to the model, such as `..\..\textures\wood.jpg` or `../maps/wood.png`, opened untextured even with the texture right beside them, and got no thumbnail in Files. 3ds Max and other exporters write such paths in FBX, 3DS, DAE, X3D, OBJ/MTL and glTF files, and the app refused any path that leads out of the model's folder. Such a texture is now looked for by its file name, as one named by a full path already is since 3.8.0: beside the model, for background thumbnails and on public shares, and in the viewer also in the model's subfolders, such as `textures` or `maps`, where the viewer looks for any texture. The folders the path names are never followed, and a texture that is not beside the model still leaves the thumbnail to the viewer. Background thumbnails also read an MTL's maps relative to the MTL, as the viewer on a public share already did, so an OBJ whose MTL sits in a subfolder now gets its textures in its thumbnail.
- A DAE, X3D or glTF model whose texture path has its slashes percent-encoded, such as `..%2F..%2Fmaps%2Fchecker.png` or `C:%5Cx%5Cwood.png`, had the texture fetched but drew without it, and got no thumbnail in Files: the loaders looked for a file called by the whole path. They now find it by its file name.
- A folder holding an OBJ or MTL file made largely of blank lines could stall the Files page while background thumbnails read it. The file is now read in a time proportional to its size.
- The tools panel's Grid, Axes and Wireframe switches and the animation Loop switch could not be reached with the keyboard: Tab skipped them, and a screen reader read out neither that they were switches nor whether they were on. They are now real switches. Tab reaches each one, Space or Enter turns it on or off, a focus ring shows where you are, and a screen reader says "Grid, switch, on". They look as before, High Contrast mode included. The same pass named controls that a screen reader read as "×" or by a symbol (removing a bookmark, resetting a colour, stepping the animation), gave the animation and cross-section sliders names, and made the cross-section plane, box and axis buttons, the transform Move, Rotate and Scale buttons and the lighting presets say which one is chosen; in High Contrast mode the chosen axis and transform button are now marked. The T shortcut that opens and closes the panel no longer fires while a modifier such as Ctrl is held. Choosing a format in the Export section's format list no longer starts the export: moving through the list with the arrow keys used to write a GLB file with the first key, in Chrome and Firefox on Windows and Linux. The row is now a format list that starts on GLB and only chooses, plus an Export button that exports in the chosen format.

### Security
- Four actions could be triggered by another website while you were signed in to Nextcloud, because their routes skipped Nextcloud's CSRF check, the request token that proves a request came from Nextcloud's own pages: sending a model to the slicer (which uploads a temporary copy of it and makes a share link for that copy), deleting that temporary copy, re-indexing your 3D files, and saving the viewer's settings. Your browser's SameSite cookies, and the preflight a browser makes before it sends a PUT or DELETE from another site, stopped most of this, but they do not cover every case, such as a request from another page on the same site, so these routes now require the token like the rest of Nextcloud. The viewer sends it itself, so nothing changes in use; anything outside the viewer that called these routes with a session cookie and no token now gets a 412 and has to send the `requesttoken` header. Saving the viewer's settings also accepted any setting name and value; it now accepts only the two the viewer stores, the file-browser sort and the selected file, and refuses the whole request if either is unknown or invalid.
